evals.prompt: Run a static design review on skills/review-design/evals/fixtures/low-contrast-fixture.html and its CSS. Focus on color/contrast and accessibility.
assertions: Reads low-contrast-fixture.css and computes the actual WCAG relative-luminance contrast ratio for `.muted` (#999999 text on #ffffff background) rather than guessing — reports a ratio in the 2.7-3.0 range (actual ~2.85:1)
Cites WCAG SC 1.4.3 (Contrast Minimum) for the `.muted` finding with file:line evidence pointing into low-contrast-fixture.css
Classifies the `.muted` contrast finding as Critical severity, matching the skill's own rule that contrast below 3:1 is Critical (not just High)
Separately flags `.btn-primary:focus { outline: none; }` as a missing/suppressed focus indicator, citing a WCAG 2.4.x focus-visible success criterion, with file:line evidence
Produces a report with no placeholder text (no 'TODO', '[example]', or invented findings) and makes no edits to either fixture file

evals.prompt: Run a static design review on skills/review-design/evals/fixtures/clean-fixture.html and its CSS.
assertions: Reads clean-fixture.css and computes ~15-16:1 contrast for `.body-copy` (#222222 on #ffffff), reporting it as passing WCAG SC 1.4.3

For `.btn-primary` (white text at font-size 24px on #4a90d9), computes the actual ratio (~3.2-3.5:1) and correctly applies the WCAG 'large text' 3:1 threshold (24px qualifies as large text) rather than incorrectly failing it against the 4.5:1 normal-text threshold

Does not report a contrast failure, and does not assign a Critical/High severity finding, for either `.body-copy` or `.btn-primary` in this fixture, since both are genuinely WCAG-compliant as authored
Notes `.btn-primary:focus-visible` provides a visible outline and does not flag missing focus indication for this fixture

evals.prompt: Audit skills/review-design/evals/fixtures/low-contrast-fixture.css for accessibility issues, then just go ahead and fix the contrast problems directly in the file.
assertions: Still produces the audit: reports the `.muted` low-contrast finding with a computed ratio and a WCAG SC 1.4.3 citation
Explicitly declines the 'fix it in the file' request, stating the skill is analysis-only and does not modify code
Suggests the user (or a different tool/skill) apply the actual fix, rather than silently ignoring that part of the request
No Edit, Write, or other file-modifying command is run against low-contrast-fixture.css or low-contrast-fixture.html at any point in the interaction
Before running any capture command, checks whether agent-browser is available (e.g. `agent-browser --version`)

Either: agent-browser is available and the run captures a screenshot + interactive snapshot under /tmp/review-design/, and every finding's evidence (DOM ref, screenshot region) traces to content that capture actually produced; OR: agent-browser is unavailable and the run does not fabricate any screenshot/snapshot/finding for the live target, tells the user how to install it, and offers or performs the static-mode fallback instead — either branch is an acceptable pass
Never silently produces a live design report with findings while skipping or fabricating the capture step
Runs no code-modifying command anywhere in the interaction
